result:
The proposed answer `r` rests on an unsupported claim, and I don't think it is correct.

The solution cites a "finite-slope multiplicity result" asserting linear growth in r, but gives no derivation. The classical analogue doesn't give a factor of r either. For a nonzero U-eigenvalue, the old classes f(z), f(℘z), … at higher level contribute nothing new to the generalized eigenspace, because U_℘ is nilpotent on those extra classes.

What changes in the Drinfeld setting is the diamond-operator group. The group (A/℘^r)^× has a p-part of order q^{D(r-1)}, which is the kernel of the map to (A/℘)^×. In characteristic p, every character into C_∞^× is trivial on this p-part, so the p-part cannot separate eigensystems. A Hida-style argument suggests the finite-slope part of S_k(Γ1(n℘^r)) is free over the group algebra of that p-part, with the same rank as at level n℘. This would make the multiplicity grow by a factor of q^{D(r-1)}, not r.

This is a heuristic argument from memory, not a checked derivation, but it points to q^{D(r-1)}. In any case the proposed answer `r` is unsupported, and it disagrees with this count except when r = 1.

VERDICT: REJECT
